title: fix: preserve automation management for queued owner messages
body:
Related: #168823 (this fixes fresh channel-owner messages queued for followup/collect execution, not every parent-resumption path).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authenticated channel owner sees only the current conversation's automations when their message waits in the followup queue.

## User Impact

Owners retain their existing ability to manage gateway-wide automations after a queued message starts; revoked ownership and non-owner or internal messages remain restricted. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original ingress capability expires before queued execution starts with a new run identity. Preserve a source-bound capability factory through queue collection and overflow, then enter a fresh scope for that queued run. The original sender, transport identity, current-owner check, and run-settlement/abort revocation remain authoritative; presentation defaults cannot supply another turn's capability.

## Related work and scope

Related: #148790 (merged channel-owner automation management) and #160018 (merged owner-authority preservation after a child reply). #148294 tracks the broader distinction between admission authority, continuation ownership, and delivered completion. This PR fixes fresh authenticated channel-owner messages crossing the followup/collect queue. The Control UI parent-resumption report #168823 enters through a different path; neither that entire issue nor the broader completion contract is claimed resolved here.

## Reproduction and environment

Observed on macOS with packaged OpenClaw 2026.10.2 and a configured Telegram channel owner. The controlled comparison restored the exact original versions of the three affected runtime modules, then applied the qualified fix; the installation also contained disclosed unrelated backports. The isolated Gateway cases used synthetic external Telegram/model endpoints. The separate October 15 Telegram check used the normal channel and provider. These runtime results belong to the earlier qualified patch, not to a new deployment of the October 16 integration head.

1. Configure an explicit owner in `commands.ownerAllowFrom` and use a Gateway with automation jobs belonging to multiple conversations. Confirm a fresh owner request can list the full inventory.
2. Start owner request A with a bounded wait. While A is still running, send a separate owner request B asking the native `automations` tool for `action=list, includeDisabled=true`, with the inline `/queue followup` directive at the end of B's message.
3. Confirm B arrives while A runs and executes afterward with a different run identity. Inspect the actual native tool result, not just the model's answer or a CLI list.
4. Before the fix, the exact-original control returns `scope=caller` with 1 of 6 jobs. After the fix, it returns `scope=gateway` with all 6; the separate real Telegram run returned all 73 jobs with `hasMore=false` and matching operator-inventory IDs.

The non-owner, foreign-source and authenticated-cancellation controls and the deferred-revocation limitation are linked below. This reproduction makes no mutation-race claim.

## Evidence

- October 16 integration: merged frozen main `0fd8396314714ed4251d802502a072ec558b9f5e` into this branch to resolve the actual import conflict. Head `534dce6504ba0438f0f76e111f09f852769b9a9e` retains both imports, and the PR's added/removed lines across all seven files are identical to the previously reviewed patch. Formatting and the diff check pass. A focused four-file test attempt stopped before tests in the borrowed compiler installation (`Symbol.dispose`); type-aware lint also refused dependencies outside this checkout. The borrowed compiler/test-runner versions differ from the new base and were not modified. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38876614603) completed successfully on `534dce6504ba0438f0f76e111f09f852769b9a9e`; the current check rollup has 69 successful, 56 skipped and 1 neutral check, with no failing or pending checks. This hosted result verifies the new integration head; the earlier runtime proof retains its stated version boundary. No local full core build or production change.

- Reproduced the loss through real ingress preparation, queue draining, followup execution, and the native cron tool before the fix, then verified gateway scope after it. External model execution and gateway transport are isolated fixtures; the capability and grant checks are real.
- On pre-integration head `e5691d669a93ada9b8dd75099d76a12292510b9c`, 130 focused tests passed: 112 prepared-reply tests, 3 queued-callback tests, and 15 queue-authority tests. The 36 new cases cover both queue modes, batching, overflow, mixed sources, current-owner revocation, sender aliases, and internal/replayed/spawned/non-owner inputs.
- On the pre-integration head above, targeted typed lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and the repository-required autoreview passed. CI exposed that a whole-object queue type annotation rejected existing private ingress metadata; the factory was captured before object construction to preserve the inferred shape. All 130 focused tests passed after this adjustment. The changed 112-test file also passed after narrowing the native tool result and preserving all real typing-module exports; two obsolete mock allowances were removed, and the mock-export ratchet passed.
- The complete [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38639828076) passes on e5691d669a93ada9b8dd75099d76a12292510b9c, including production/test declarations, lint, extension-package boundaries, and baseline ratchets. Local declaration checks could not use the borrowed dependency installation; CI provides that verification. No local full core build. The packaged-Gateway negative controls below use synthetic external services; the additional real Telegram check uses the normal channel and model provider.

- Additional packaged-Gateway proof: with exact-original negative control, a queued owner returns `caller/1` before and `gateway/6` after; fixed output IDs exactly match the global inventory, including foreign-agent jobs. Native ingress, queue, tool, grants, Gateway transport and handlers are real; only external Telegram/model endpoints are fixtures.
- Nearest forbidden paths: non-owner tool surface excludes automations; a different local agent-RPC source without channel-owner/Control UI management entitlement returns `caller/1` and no foreign jobs; authenticated `/stop` after queued tool binding prevents automation execution or result. Config-only owner removal was deferred by channel reload and is not counted as applied-revocation proof. No mutation-race claim. [The evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172539#issuecomment-6179957120) contains the redacted native trace and boundaries.


- Real Telegram owner-channel check (October 15): B arrived while A was executing a bounded command and ran afterward with its own run identity using a per-message followup directive. Its actual native `automations` list result was `scope=gateway`, `total=73`, 73 returned, `hasMore=false`, with every job ID matching the operator inventory. The reply was delivered to Telegram; persistent queue mode stayed unchanged. This proves the production read path, not a new revocation or mutation-commit race.
